title: I built TrenchersAI because “the AI decided” is not a good enough explanation when money is involved
author: CODE_HEIST
selftext:
I built TrenchersAI, an AI-native trading terminal where traders can describe a strategy, turn it into an agent, and test it in Paper mode before going Live.

Getting an agent to place a trade was not the hardest part.

The hard part was answering what happened afterward.

* what did the agent see?
* which entry checks passed?
* why did it reject a token?
* which strategy version was running?
* what changed between two versions?
* which risk rules should the agent never be allowed to change?

Most trading products make the winning screenshot easy to share. I wanted TrenchersAI to make the boring decisions visible too.

So I built the workflow around inspectability.

* Watch Feed shows candidates and individual checks
* entry gates separate holders, unique wallets, concentration, developer exposure and re-entry
* every agent has its own positions and transaction history
* configuration changes are versioned
* Paper and Live environments are clearly separated
* traders can remain manual, use AI assistance, or delegate a defined setup

The most useful output is not always a buy.

Sometimes it is an explainable no.

If an agent rejects a launch because ownership is too concentrated or wallet activity does not match the setup, that decision should be inspectable. If its configuration changes, future results should be connected to the new version instead of being mixed with the old one.

Important context. The attached screens are from Paper mode. Simulated results do not prove an edge. Passing filters does not make a token safe, and AI does not remove liquidity, execution or contract risk.

[TrenchersAI](https://trenchers.ai/) is live and I’m still working through the trust layer.

For people building or using trading agents, what would you require before trusting one live?

Immutable risk limits? Clear rejection reasons? Full position reconciliation? Human approval before strategy changes? Something else?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
an explainable no is the right thing to build around and almost nobody does, because nobody screenshots a rejection.

the version I'd extend it to is the data, not just the config. if an entry gate reads holder concentration from a provider and that provider quietly changes how it counts, your config is unchanged and the decision moves anyway. hashing the input snapshot next to the config version is what makes a rerun that disagrees tell you which of the two actually moved.

replies.author: CODE_HEIST
replies.body:
tbh, that’s a gap in how I framed it. an unchanged config can still produce a different decision if the provider changes what a field means.

i’d want to preserve the actual input snapshot, source and timestamp alongside the config version and hash then there’s something to inspect when two runs disagree.

have you dealt with providers changing their definitions in practice? curious how you caught it when the response format stayed the same.
